alias.note: the draw id the wrapper ran under

alias_err.note: kept in the report, first 300 characters

alias_rc.note: alias_rc != 0 means the wrapper fell back to the lineage's own id: reported (K18)

best_generic_in_shape.note: R-46, named by the ruling: the best generic rule per shape, chosen and scored on the same items

oracle_any_literal.reason: R-46: its value uses the answers of the items it is scored on (an oracle or a best-of choice made and scored on the same items); not a rule

shapes.note: items per shape, for the recovery of MF_shape_cv

per_level.note: {level: {rule: share of the level}}; 4 decimals; a rule with no hit at a level is not written

c1_s5.files: s5.json (audit4_c1/s5_analyse_v2.py), source 'a4' of the class table

EFF_F.note: counts as written, whole (point 6, K8): its components cannot be read apart

EFF_SM.note: read; left uncounted only by the class table (measure equal on EFF_SM)

MFsh.note: most frequent key per shape, 2-fold CV; 3 decimals

rules.note: {'<shape>|<rule>': row}; the rule is the part after the first '|'

shapes.note: shape sizes; each rule row carries its own n_shape

rate_in_shape.note: hits of the shape = round(rate_in_shape x n_shape), summed over the shapes (R-34; the text's reading); 3 decimals

share_of_level.note: read only for the report: f4b_pool_v2.py recovers hits as round(share_of_level x n); the report lists rules whose decision would change under it

answer_echoed_anywhere.reason: R-46: its value uses the answers of the items it is scored on (an oracle or a best-of choice made and scored on the same items); not a rule

best_echo.note: names of the echo rules chosen on the held-out halves

rates.note: {key: rate}; named as written (they already carry a4: or im:)

within_applicable.reason: K7: not a rule; the rate over the items a rule applies to

answer_echoed_anywhere.note: whether the answer occurs among the numbers of the question, counted over the scored items
answer_echoed_anywhere.reason: R-46: its value uses the answers of the items it is scored on (an oracle or a best-of choice made and scored on the same items); not a rule

base.note: held-out rate of the most frequent answer; read as the rule 'most frequent answer' against chance and as the second base (point 7)

halfwidth95.reason: derived: a half-width, not a rule's figure

minus_base.reason: derived: rates less base, formed by the pooling script from the two pooled figures

mode_insample.note: the commonest answer's rate among the scored items themselves
mode_insample.reason: R-46: its value uses the answers of the items it is scored on (an oracle or a best-of choice made and scored on the same items); not a rule

rates.note: {key: rate}; named 'im:' + key; keys ending __within_applicable are not rules (K7)

a3_skipped_items.note: items on which an audit-3 rule raised; section a3 only

exclusions.note: the original's list of procedure exclusions; classes come from the class table only

raw.note: sections own, a4 and a3, each {lid: {level: row, a3_skipped_items}}

seeds.reason: not the true seeds: the literals of the original (410302, 17, 5) are written whatever the seeds were (K15); seeds are taken from the plan

summary.reason: derived: the script's own maxima over the same rates; the pooling script forms every figure itself

asked_is_largest_observed_vs_uniform.reason: K7: not a rule; a diagnostic of the answer's position (ratio_share only)

minus_base.reason: derived: formed by the pooling script from the two pooled figures

one_op_best.reason: K7: not a rule; names of the operands chosen

rates.note: {key: rate}; named as written; rounded to 5 decimals; keys ending __within_applicable are not rules (K7)

N.note: the item count asked for; each row's N is read

seed.reason: seeds are taken from the plan, and this is the same integer

acc_fired.note: read only to list exact rows (point 8): accuracy on the items it answered; None when it never fired

anti.note: the gain from choosing among the options the rule did not pick; None for an open answer and for the fitted lookups; read as an excess of its own

chance.note: eff is already the excess over chance (point 7), so chance is not needed

eff.note: already the rate less chance, rounded to 4 decimals by the script (pooled as the item-weighted mean of the written figures)

fired.note: read only to list exact rows (point 8): items on which the rule answered

heuristic.note: the rule's name as written; one rule = one name in one kind of file of one unit for one lineage

lineage.note: mapped to the survivor-list id by the plan's id map; a lineage that is not on the map is not read

mode_rate.note: R1b audit rows only: the rate of the commonest answer among the scored items themselves (heuristics4.py:634). Under R-46 it is not a rule; the fitted constant rule constant_mfk_fitted is a row of its own and is read
mode_rate.reason: R-46: its value uses the answers of the items it is scored on (an oracle or a best-of choice made and scored on the same items); not a rule

n.note: the row's own item count (1,000 per level for the R1a fitted lookups, as the text says)

r1c_stdout.files: stdout.txt: one line per lineage and rule, f"{lid:36s} {h[:60]:60s} eff " + 7 values with +.3f + "   anti " + 7 values (new_rules_final.py, last line)

anti_values.note: exactly 7 values, levels 0 to 6; same uncertainty

eff_values.note: exactly 7 values, levels 0 to 6; 4-decimal rounding then 3-decimal printing: uncertainty 0.00055 (point 7)

item_count.note: the script writes none; the plan's items per level is used (R1c, point 8 last bullet: no row can be set aside)

rule_name.note: cut to 60 characters by the script; read as printed (trailing blanks removed)

acc_all.reason: derived: k / n of the shape, which the script forms itself from k and n

acc_app.reason: derived: k / napp, which the script forms itself from k and napp

napp.note: items on which the rule gives an answer

nerr.note: items on which the rule raised; the script counts them as no answer, which k and napp already reflect

answer_type.note: yn gives the base 0.5 and the statistic k/napp; list, number and text give the base 0

n.note: items of the shape (the test draw); summed over the shapes of the level

rules.note: {rule name: counts}; R2a writes no rule with napp = 0, R2b writes every rule

lineages.note: {lid: {level: {shape: ...}}}; lid mapped by the plan's id map

n.note: the item count the script was asked for; each shape's own n is read

seeds.note: a literal description or tag of the original, not the seed; seeds are taken from the plan

rulings.K7: M1: keys ending __within_applicable, within_applicable, one_op_best and asked_is_largest_observed_vs_uniform are not rules and are not read.
rulings.R-46: A field is a rule only if its prediction for an item can be computed without that item's answer. oracle_any_literal (both C1 outputs) and best_generic_in_shape (C1 battery) are not read; MF_printform_cv counts; BEST_generic_cv counts; share_of_level in the a3 output is not a hit share and hits are read from hit.
